items.title: Understanding Automated Program Repair Agents through the Lens of Traceability: An Empirical Study
items.abstract: Automated Program Repair (APR) agents leverage large language models (LLMs) to autonomously diagnose and patch software bugs using planning, reasoning, and tools. Although these agents show strong performance on leaderboards such as SWE-bench, little is understood about how they take actions, where they fail, and how their behavior compares to human developers. In this paper, we present the first systematic analysis of these limitations using 5 state-of-the-art APR agents. We trace the full decision-making pipelines of the 5 APR agents across 500 real-world repair tasks, from issue description to patch validation. Our study reveals that, while agents excel at simple fixes, they struggle with logic-intensive bugs, often generating verbose, overfitted patches that pass existing test suites without solving the root cause. Test generation and regression test selection remain major bottlenecks, as agents fail to reproduce issues or run relevant regression tests. Moreover, many agents operate with primitive tooling (e.g. bash scripts) and do not have access to debuggers or program analysis tools. These findings highlight key limitations of current APR systems and motivate several directions for next-generation APR design, including but not limited to: (1) a shift-left approach emphasizing early, high-quality test generation and validation to reduce spurious fixes and improve semantic correctness; (2) richer, more integrated tool ecosystems; (3) diversified agent architectures that combine complementary strengths; and (4) benchmarks that prioritize semantic repair quality and test-generation fidelity over surface-level success metrics.

items.title: Understanding Learner Engagement and Persistence in AI-Assisted Interactive Climate Fiction Learning
items.abstract: Advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled educators to create increasingly sophisticated interactive learning materials, yet relatively little research has examined how learners engage with and persist in such interventions over time. This exploratory case study investigated learner engagement and persistence within a five-stage AI-assisted interactive climate fiction (cli-fi) intervention delivered through H5P activities embedded within the Moodle learning management system as part of an extracurricular sustainability initiative at an English-medium university in China. Participation, activity scores, completion data, and time-on-task measures were analysed descriptively across a five-week intervention. While learners who engaged with the intervention demonstrated high levels of engagement, reflected in strong activity scores and substantial interaction with the materials, participation declined markedly across successive stages, falling from 25 learners in Story 1 to six learners by Story 5. Descriptive improvements were observed in environmental knowledge scores among the small number of learners completing both pre- and post-tests, although these findings were inconclusive. The findings highlight a clear distinction between engagement and persistence, suggesting that engaging digital learning experiences do not necessarily translate into sustained participation. The study contributes to emerging research on AI-assisted learning design by emphasising the importance of considering persistence as a distinct outcome when designing and evaluating multi-stage digital learning environments.

items.title: Unpacking AI Agent Participation in Issue-Centered Collaboration in Open-Source Software Development
items.abstract: The increasing participation of AI agents in open-source software development raises questions about their role in collaborative processes. This paper investigates how AI agent participation relates to the structure and outcomes of issue-centered collaboration in open-source software projects. We adopt a process-level perspective by modeling issue handling as sequences of events and extending dynamic issue-pr entropy to distinguish between agent-related and non-agent-related contributions. Using large-scale issue event data from 83 GitHub repositories, we construct a project–month panel dataset and analyze associations between collaboration complexity and development outcomes. Our results show that agent-related collaboration complexity is more strongly associated with development output than human-only collaboration complexity, and is associated with fewer newly introduced defects. In contrast, its relationship with issue resolution efficiency is highly context-dependent. These findings highlight the importance of considering collaboration structure when evaluating the impact of AI agents in open-source software development.

items.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning methods for Analysing Acoustic Emission data
items.abstract: The foundation of track construction in Germany and many other countries is typically based on a gravel superstructure with railway sleepers made of prestressed concrete. Concrete has been approved as a material for sleeper construction for several decades. However, sleepers are exposed to weather conditions and changing temperatures, which can lead to erosion processes. Artificial intelligence methods have been successfully applied to locate cracking events in concrete structures. Typically, supervised learning is used to train deep neural networks on events identified by traditional triangulation methods. In this work, self-supervised methods are applied to raw acoustic emission data to evaluate information without prior labeling. We compare autoencoders that create rich latent space embeddings of the events with results achieved by using Self-Organizing Maps and traditional clustering on vectors created through feature engineering of the signals. This study analyzes data from over 19,000 events with 16 channels of sound recordings obtained in a static three-point bending test with railway sleepers. The high dimensional latent space can be visualized with dimension reduction techniques. This evaluation of the manifold of the embedded vectors indicates that location information is preserved by this embedding process.

items.title: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) in vegetable crops: A review
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging technology in vegetable production, enabling data-driven decision making and precision agriculture practices. AI refers to the intelligence exhibited by machines that can perceive their environment, process large datasets, and make decisions to optimize agricultural productivity. With the integration of technologies such as machine learning, sensors, drones, satellites, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Global Positioning Systems (GPS), AI enables efficient monitoring and management of crop production systems In vegetable cultivation, AI technologies assist farmers in several critical operations including soil monitoring, climate assessment, pest and disease diagnosis, irrigation scheduling, and yield prediction. Sensors such as wind vane, cup count anemometer, rain gauge, lux meter, soil moisture sensor, and crop canopy sensors collect real-time environmental and crop data. These data was processed through data loggers and machine learning algorithms to provide accurate recommendations for crop management. Drone-based imaging systems and multispectral cameras further support precision farming by identifying weeds, nutrient deficiencies and disease symptoms at early stages. The use of AI in vegetables also highlights image-based predictive agriculture systems where captured images are processed through stages such as. image cleaning, feature extraction, and model training to detect pests and diseases. Several case studies demonstrate the use of AI in vegetable crops such as tomato, capsicum, and chilli for monitoring canopy growth, irrigation management. Additionally, robotic technologies in harvesting address labor shortages in agriculture. items.title: User Beware: Inaccuracy and Inconsistency of Large Language Models in Providing Precision Dosing Recommendations for Patients With Kidney Impairment—A Case Series
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence-based dosing guidance for medications in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) and receiving continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) is limited. Freely available large language models (LLMs) can generate confident, human-like outputs. The accuracy and reproducibility of LLMs in providing precision drug dosing recommendations in the setting of AKI and CKRT have not been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: We sought to characterize literature concordance and internal consistency of LLM-generated dosing recommendations for cefepime and meropenem in patients with AKI and receiving CKRT. METHODS: Six investigators queried the freely available versions of six LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, OpenEvidence, and Perplexity) from July to September 2025 using three standardized vignettes asking for dosing recommendations and rationale to meet prespecified pharmacodynamic targets: (i) adult with AKI not on dialysis receiving cefepime, (ii) child receiving CKRT and cefepime, and (iii) toddler receiving high-effluent CKRT and meropenem. To assess inter-iteration consistency, each investigator also prompted one LLM three times for each vignette. Responses were parsed for concordance with recommendations in primary literature. LLM "reasoning" was evaluated for use of pharmacokinetic (PK) equations, citation accuracy versus confabulation, acknowledgment of uncertainty, and recommendations for therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) for efficacy or safety. RESULTS: LLM-generated dosing recommendations varied widely. Mean concordance with literature-based recommendations was 63% (range: 28%-94%). LLMs produced variable responses to the same user upon multiple iterations, with variance in daily maintenance doses recommended ranging from 0 to 1000%. OpenEvidence universally cited relevant sources, whereas other LLMs leveraged sources inconsistently or confabulated them. Each recommended TDM, though only Claude consistently acknowledged its own uncertainty. CONCLUSION: Freely available LLMs produce highly variable and often discordant antibiotic dosing recommendations for patients with AKI and receiving CKRT. Although valuable for hypothesis generation and literature retrieval, LLM outputs should not be used in isolation for drug dosing in critically ill patients with kidney dysfunction.

items.title: Using artificial intelligence to mitigate global teacher shortage
items.abstract: Purpose This viewpoint addresses the systemic global teacher crisis – driven by burnout, unsustainable workloads and administrative attrition – and explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to reduce non-academic tasks. This piece argues that by using AI to help with administrative burdens, education systems can improve teacher retention, enhance individual student engagement and even support democracy. Design/methodology/approach This piece uses a conceptual and synthesis-based approach, combining a review of current literature with the author's firsthand narrative reflections as a veteran educator and teacher trainer. Findings The piece identifies the root causes of the teacher shortage: the overwhelming volume of non-instructional work. The analysis of the literature supports the use of AI tools to unburden teachers from non-instructional work gaining time to build robust relationships with students, increase the individualization of instruction, all of which can lead to better meeting the learning needs of their students. Finally, it allows for a better life–work balance that can mitigate teacher attrition and attract more quality candidates. Research limitations/implications This is a viewpoint article, and although it is supported by a robust review of relevant literature, it does not put forward new empirical evidence. Practical implications The practical implications of the piece focus on reforming the daily operations of educators' work by integrating AI to eliminate up to six hours of administrative workload per week, thereby reducing teacher burnout and mitigating the global shortage. Social implications The social implications center on safeguarding democratic foundations by stabilizing an endangered education system. Restoring work–life balance through AI helps attract and retain qualified teachers, preventing the systemic collapse of public schooling. Originality/value The originality of this piece is in its unique view of how to mitigate the teacher shortage by embracing AI tools rather than fear them. By using relevant national and international literature in conjunction with the authentic, lived perspective of a veteran educator, the piece provides a fresh approach to combatting the teacher shortage.

items.title: Validating LLM-Generated Expert Judgments in AHP Decision Support: A Preregistered Cross-Study Benchmark and Randomized-Order Audit
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering decision-support systems as inexpensive synthetic experts, yet their judgments are rarely validated against published human targets. We benchmark six LLMs on a source-audited corpus of 27 published Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) studies with a preregistered holdout of 22 studies, 21 reference-weight tasks, 28,783 valid benchmark calls, and study-clustered inference. Holdout rank replication was modest and model dependent. A diagnostic showed that fixed-source-order rank evaluation is confounded with criterion presentation order: reference vectors largely follow source listing order, and a model-free descending-order rule reaches a mean Spearman correlation of 0.735, outscoring every model. A prospective randomized-order experiment raised Claude Sonnet 5’s mean Spearman correlation by 0.46, and a registered follow-up with an exactly balanced schedule replicated that gain. For HCX-007, the model that tracks presentation order most strongly, the randomized-order decline was directional but not statistically significant (0.17, Holm p=0.16), and the follow-up was inconclusive about the average difference (+0.007, 95% CI [−0.23, 0.22]); its single draws continued to follow presentation order, and in an exploratory subgroup of six tasks with seven or more criteria its balanced-order accuracy was lower. Most holdout panels could be implemented only as repeated draws under a shared profile, and matched individual human data were limited to two tasks. Benchmarks for synthetic experts should therefore balance presentation order and evaluate aggregate reconstruction, individual human-likeness, and downstream ranking separately.

items.title: Virtual Mourning in the Metaverse: User Acceptance, Needs, and Limitations of AI-Based Memory Avatars
items.abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly shaping the ways in which people remember and grieve. While existing platforms and social networks primarily preserve static content, immersive environments such as the metaverse and advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) enable the creation of interactive, AI-based memory avatars, often also referred to as “griefbots” or “deadbots”. This study examines the perceptions, acceptance, opportunities, as well as psychosocial and ethical limitations of such avatars from the perspective of potential users. To provide an empirical foundation, an interactive prototype was developed and evaluated as part of a quantitative study (N = 33). These results were supplemented by qualitative guided interviews with experts in grief counseling, psychotherapy, and pastoral care. The findings paint a highly ambivalent picture: While respondents see potential in preserving life stories or in processing missed goodbyes, concerns regarding emotional dependence, difficulties in accepting loss, and ethical and data protection risks dominate. The Behavioral Intention to use the technology depends largely on Perceived Usefulness (r = 0.74) and Emotional Impact (r = 0.82), rather than purely on user interface elements. Experts emphasize that simulated interactions must not hinder the necessary process of letting go. The study concludes with recommendations for transparency requirements, time limits, and clear ethical safeguards for vulnerable groups.

items.title: Which Evaluation Strategies Help Students Spot Visual Misinformation on Social Media?
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The rapid spread of visual misinformation online, intensified by advances in generative artificial intelligence, presents new challenges for adolescents' digital information literacy. Although students' difficulties in evaluating online information are well documented, little is known about how they assess different forms of visual misinformation on social media. Objectives This study examined the extent to which lower secondary school students can successfully identify different types of visual misinformation on social media, the evaluation strategies they use, and whether these strategies predict misinformation detection across types of visual misinformation. Methods The participants were 272 students in Grades 7–9 who evaluated social media posts containing visual misinformation, including manipulated videos, manipulated images, and AI‐generated images. Students rated each item's credibility and provided written justifications. Evaluation strategies were coded using a theoretically grounded scheme. Results Students were moderately successful in identifying manipulated images and videos, but struggled to detect AI‐generated images, which were often perceived as credible. Students relied primarily on evaluation of visual appearance and content, while source evaluation and corroboration strategies were infrequently used. Across all visual misinformation types, examination of visual features, knowledge‐based evaluation, sourcing, and corroboration strategies predicted misinformation detection. However, corroboration was the only strategy that reliably predicted identification of AI‐generated images. Conclusions Students mostly rely on first‐hand evaluation of visual appearance and content, but these strategies are inadequate for detecting realistic AI‐generated visual misinformation. Instruction should emphasize active verification strategies, particularly corroboration, and support students in coordinating multiple evaluation strategies when engaging with online visual information.

items.title: WHY PYTHON PROGRAMMING IN PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCE?
items.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of the pharmaceutical sector has created a growing demand for professionals who can combine pharmaceutical knowledge with computational and data-analytic skills. Python programming has emerged as a valuable educational and professional tool because of its simple syntax, open-source nature, extensive scientific libraries, and applicability in data analysis, visualization, automation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacovigilance, formulation research, clinical studies, bioinformatics, quality control, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug development. The revised B.Pharm curriculum introduced by the Pharmacy Council of India under the NEP 2020 framework recognizes this changing professional environment by including Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences at the undergraduate level. This curricular development represents an important shift from conventional computer literacy toward structured programming, pharmaceutical data handling, scientific visualization, and computational problem-solving. The present review examines the rationale for incorporating Python programming into pharmaceutical education and correlates the revised curriculum with emerging requirements of the pharmaceutical industry. Particular emphasis is placed on the relevance of NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, data cleaning, CSV/Excel processing, pharmacokinetic datasets, adverse drug reaction analysis, dissolution-profile visualization, research data management, and introductory pathways toward machine learning and artificial intelligence. The review further discusses the potential contribution of Python competency to pharmaceutical research and development, quality assurance, manufacturing, regulatory science, clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and Pharma 4.0. Challenges related to faculty training, infrastructure, limited instructional hours, data integrity, validation, and responsible use of artificial intelligence are also considered. It is concluded that Python should not be regarded merely as an additional programming subject in the pharmacy curriculum, but as a foundational digital competency capable of improving data literacy, research capability, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industrial readiness among future pharmacy graduates. This article cover subject wisr role of python programming in pharmaceutical industries.

items.title: Wildlife Monitoring System Using GSM System
items.abstract: The increasing incidence of wild animal intrusion in agricultural areas poses significant risks to both human safety and crop productivity. This project, AI-IoT Smart Animal Surveillance for Human Safety, proposes a real-time monitoring system that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Internet of Things (IoT) to detect, alert, and assess the presence of wild animals near farms. The system utilises a Raspberry Pi equipped with a camera module and employs the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm to accurately identify animals from live video feeds. Upon detection, the system captures the image, sends an email alert with timestamp and location to the farmer, and activates a buzzer to warn nearby individuals. Additionally, IoT-based health monitoring sensors such as temperature, heartbeat, and gas sensors are used to evaluate the physical condition and surrounding environment of the detected animals, aiding early detection of diseases or environmental threats. The system operates in real-time and ensures quick response to critical situations, thereby minimizing crop damage and reducing the risk of human-animal conflicts. It is designed to be cost-effective, energy-efficient, and easy to deploy in rural and remote areas. Furthermore, the system can be enhanced with features such as mobile application integration, cloud-based data storage, and GPS tracking for better monitoring and control. Overall, the proposed system provides a smart, automated, and reliable solution for wildlife surveillance and safety management.

items.title: Workplace health investment and employment adjustment public health evidence from CSR reports of Chinese A-share listed firms
items.abstract: This study examines whether workplace-health-related corporate practices disclosed in corporate social responsibility (CSR) reports are associated with firm-level employment adjustment. Using 12,669 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2024, we construct a sentence-level measure of CSR-disclosed workplace health practice intensity and relate it to employment growth and residual employment-adjustment volatility. The indicator captures the relative intensity of disclosed occupational health and safety, medical support, mental-health services, health promotion and working-condition improvements. In firm and year fixed-effects models, a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure intensity is associated with approximately 2.4% points higher employment growth and 0.012 higher three-year adjustment volatility. The associations are accompanied by lower disclosed work-injury rates and employee turnover, and the volatility pattern is concentrated in positive residual adjustment and industry upturns. Instrumental-variable and sample-selection analyses yield estimates consistent with the baseline fixed-effects results and the proposed occupational-health service channel. The results support an interpretation of lower occupational-health-related labor frictions and stronger expansion-oriented employment responsiveness. The study contributes evidence on the labor-market implications of corporate resource allocation toward workplace health governance and provides a firm-level basis for further health-economic evaluation.

items.title: Zenodo Metadata — Be: Founding Business Proposal v2.0
items.abstract: Be is a proposed organization dedicated to making safe, professionally governed artificial intelligence emotional support freely accessible to people who need someone to talk to. Be proposes an AI emotional-support system designed around a foundational distinction: an AI must never confuse what it observes with what it infers. Version 2.0 further develops the proposal's framework for adaptive conversational communication through the principle Adaptive Tone, Fixed Boundaries. Be may adapt its tone, vocabulary, pacing, humor, warmth, and conversational style to meet an individual where they are, while maintaining fixed ethical and relational boundaries. The system should allow human-like communication without creating a false human identity, adapting the interface without fabricating the relationship. The proposal incorporates Red Tape Theory™ as a proposed safety methodology: Observe. Record. Question. Do not force the axiom. Interpretation must never be represented as observation. Be does not propose to diagnose users or replace licensed mental-health professionals. Instead, it proposes a professionally governed pathway through which an AI system may recognize when AI-only support may no longer be an appropriate level of support and facilitate access to human care. A proposed charitable human-care program, If You Get It, You Get It, would seek to use charitable resources to help people access licensed professional care when professionally established safety criteria indicate that additional human support may be appropriate. Version 2.0 expands the proposal's treatment of personalization as a safety boundary, including the distinction between adapting communication to an individual and constructing a misleading simulated relationship. It also addresses clinical governance, privacy, autonomy, human handoff, crisis safety, documentation, intellectual-property considerations, research and evaluation, and a potential future child-focused system provisionally called NewBee. items.abstract: Работната бележка продължава „Защо пирамидата на доходите в България е толкова стръмна“ и „Бързи институции, бавни структури“. Те стигат до извод в три стъпки: изоставането в производителността е вътре в отраслите и е най-голямо при местните фирми; при нововъведенията то е най-голямо в организацията на работата, а не в продуктите; вероятна причина е прекъснатият частен организационен капитал. Самото управление обаче не е измерено пряко. Бележката пита дали публичните институции могат да намалят времето и цената за придобиване на организационен капитал, без да заместват пазарния подбор. Предлага „институционална инфраструктура за организационен капитал“: доброволна диагностика, стандартни управленски инструменти, практическо консултиране, по-малка административна тежест за участниците и помощ при преструктуриране, продажба или прекратяване на фирмата. Показва, че процедурата по стабилизация в Търговския закон съществува от 2017 г., но между 2017 и 2022 г. е използвана само 12 пъти. Два полеви експеримента подкрепят управленското консултиране, но ефектите силно се различават между програмите. Затова бележката не предлага национална програма, а три пилота с предварително заявени критерии за оценка и прекратяване. Подготвена с помощта на ChatGPT (OpenAI) и Claude (Anthropic); числата са сверени с посочените източници. Пълен текст на български. This working note follows two earlier notes on Bulgaria's income distribution and on the historical layers of its economy. They reach a three-step conclusion: the productivity gap lies within sectors and is largest among domestically controlled firms; in innovation, the gap is widest in the organisation of work rather than in products; a likely cause is the interrupted stock of private organisational capital, although management itself has not been measured directly. The note asks whether public institutions can reduce the time and cost of acquiring organisational capital without replacing market selection. It proposes an "institutional infrastructure for organisational capital": voluntary firm diagnostics, standard management tools, practical consulting, lower administrative burden for participants, and help with restructuring, transfer or exit. It shows that Bulgaria's pre-insolvency stabilisation procedure has existed since 2017 but was used only 12 times between 2017 and 2022. Two field experiments support management consulting, but effects vary widely across programmes. The note therefore proposes three pilots with pre-registered evaluation and termination criteria rather than a national programme. Prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic). Full text in Bulgarian.

items.title: A brief study of Tribal Brick Workers: Special reference of Thane district
items.abstract: Abstract- Brick’s manufacturing is an important industry in India. Bricks are very important raw material required in construction. Thousands of construction projects are ongoing in Mumbai Economic zone and thane district. Bricks manufacturers in thane district are primary suppliers of bricks to these construction sites. Large number of tribal communities from thane district are engaged as bricks worker in Bricks manufacturing Industry. These Tribal Brick workers play an important role in the construction industry, providing the foundation for buildings, homes, and other infrastructure projects. Despite their significant contribution, they have very challenging lives. Harsh physical labour, prolong working hours, and limited resources is an everyday issue for these workers. These tribal workers have lack of formal education, which limits their employment opportunities outside the brick industry. These workers Often employed on a seasonal basis, with very low wages, long working hours, and. Due to illiteracy and poor economic condition times, they often exploited by their owners. This article will focus on the working and living conditions of brick workers in the Thane district. This research aims to understand the socio-economic status and problems, occupational health issues, and the impact of their work environment on their overall well-being of Tribal Bricks Wokers. This paper is going to focus on the problems and possible remedies to address the various issues of Tribal Brick Workers. This research will be helpful to the broader discourse on informal labours problems and provides a foundation for policymakers and social organizations to address the challenges faced by brick workers.

items.title: A Fatigue-Gated Hold on Outbound Messages: A Technical Note for Communication-Platform-as-a-Service (CPaaS) Systems
items.abstract: When a person approves an action while tired, the AI agent that carries it out may send a message that cannot be taken back, a refund, an alert, an account change. This note suggests a simple fix: before sending, check if the approving person showed signs of fatigue. If so, hold the message briefly for a second look before it goes out. This applies to any communication platform that sends such messages on behalf of a human or an AI agent, including Zoho CPaaS, Twilio, and Infobip.

items.title: A federated explainable artificial intelligence architecture for multimodal disaster intelligence and response coordination
items.abstract: Natural disasters demand rapid synthesis of fragmented, heterogeneous data often distributed across independently governed organizations. This paper introduces DisasterAI, a federated, cloud-native, and multi-modal AI architecture for disaster intelligence. Unlike centralized analytics platforms, DisasterAI emphasizes federated data ingestion, modular adapters, and the alignment of derived intelligence—enabling cross-agency coordination without requiring raw data consolidation. The architecture integrates satellite imagery (optical and SAR), IoT sensor streams, public alerts, and contextual civic data into a unified, explainable decision-support pipeline. DisasterAI addresses critical challenges in disaster intelligence, including spatial-temporal alignment of asynchronous data, modality-aware fusion, uncertainty representation, and fairness-aware decision-making. Designed to support the entire disaster lifecycle—from early warning and forecast-informed risk analysis to impact assessment and response prioritization—it operates within a human-in-the-loop decision-support context. A scenario-driven evaluation illustrates how DisasterAI enhances coordination effectiveness, improves prioritization consistency, and maintains robustness under partial data availability. By focusing on architectural behavior and operational integration rather than algorithmic benchmarking, this work positions federated, explainable AI systems as a viable foundation for scalable and reliable disaster-response frameworks in complex, data-constrained environments.

items.title: A Feminist Stylistic study of AI-Generated and Human-Written Short Stores: A Comparative Study
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI raises serious questions about potential differences in story construction between human and AI narratives, particularly in terms of cultural and social artifacts. The research addresses the gap in feminist stylistic studies on AI-generated fiction by conducting a comparative analysis of feminist representations in AI-generated and human-written fiction. By analyzing these narratives, the current research sheds light on the extent to which AI-generated short stories stylistically compare to human-written short stories in terms of feminism. The research is guided by two questions: How do the linguistic choices used in AI-generated and human-written short stories, when analyzed through a feminist lens, reflect or challenge patriarchal thinking? And what are the main similarities and differences between AI-generated and human-written short stories in respect to feminist portrayal? The analysis employs Mills' (1995) feminist stylistic model, with emphasis on endearment terms, metaphor, transitivity, fragmentation, and focalization. The research examines one human-written short story titled Dinner Conversation (2020) and one AI-generated short story titled The Crack in the Bowl (2026) using a carefully standardized prompting process. The findings indicate that both stories perpetuate traditional gender hierarchies, albeit through diverse linguistic mechanisms. According to the research, AI, specifically ChatGPT-5.2, is more progressive in terms of gendered assumptions than the human author. In human-written stories, patriarchy is more pervasive and stable, whereas in AI-generated stories, it is more nuanced and sometimes contradictory. This research adds to the emerging studies on AI storytelling by demonstrating how AI-generated fiction can both duplicate and disrupt traditional gender stereotypes.

items.title: A framework for institutional change in the age of AI
items.abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping STEM higher education. Not only are our educational practices changing, but how we think about educational transformation must also adapt. Existing models of institutional change in STEM, aimed at interactive engagement, have largely followed an adoption logic: relatively stable, well-researched educational practices are evaluated and then scaled. These assumptions do not hold for generative AI, which is an arrival technology – entering classrooms before a sufficient pedagogical evidence base could form, and requiring institutions to act under uncertainty. Building on recent decades of work on STEM education institutional change, we propose a framework identifying six dimensions along which prior models of change must be adapted in light of AI: three concerning the tools at the center of reform (the tool’s evidence base, rate of change, and scope), and three concerning the people involved in change (faculty, change agents, and students). For each dimension, we examine how AI-era assumptions differ from those underlying prior STEM education reforms and derive design implications, including: privileging humble and local inquiries; organizing reform around pedagogical approaches rather than specific tools; repositioning change agents as facilitators of collective inquiry; and engaging students as partners in reform. Collectively, the six dimensions and design implications constitute a framework for adapting change models to support institutions under conditions of genuine uncertainty. Finally, we illustrate how the framework may be applied through a brief case-study of a faculty workshop series carried out in a university physics department to support instructors adapting to this modern AI era.

items.title: A Generative AI Framework to Predict Cardiomyocyte Contraction Function From Single Static Images
items.abstract: Understanding how cardiomyocyte structure governs contractile function is fundamental to cardiac biology and disease modeling, yet current approaches rely on time‐resolved imaging and computationally intensive analysis. Here, we present a generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework that directly predicts contractile behavior of human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC‐CMs) from single static images. Our approach integrates a U‐Net‐based generator with a patch‐based generative adversarial network (GAN) discriminator to translate morphological and sarcomere structural features into pixel‐resolved contraction heatmaps. To further enhance performance and generalizability, we incorporated synthetic cell–function pairs generated via a StyleGAN2 framework, improving prediction accuracy and perceptual similarity. Region‐specific and whole‐cell analyses revealed that AI predictions capture biologically meaningful structure–function relationships, with sarcomere organization strongly associated with both contractile output and prediction fidelity. Reconstruction error emerged as an interpretable metric reflecting localized inefficiencies in sarcomere‐to‐contraction coupling. Together, this framework establishes a scalable, interpretable strategy for inferring cardiomyocyte function from static morphology, eliminating the need for time‐lapse imaging, and positions generative AI as a powerful tool for bridging cellular structure and function to advance high‐throughput phenotyping and in vitro cardiac modeling.

items.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Website Detection Using URL and Host-Based Features with Leakage-Resistant Stacking
items.abstract: One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. Its leakage-resistant design enables unbiased evaluation and real-world applicability in cybersecurity. This work contributes to phishing detection research through hybrid ensemble learning with an emphasis on methodological rigor and extensive performance evaluation.

items.title: A latent-space extrapolation grade built into graph atomic cluster expansion foundation potentials
items.abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials cover broad configurational and chemical spaces, but their reliability can vary across the atomic environments encountered during a simulation. Here we introduce the calibrated Mahalanobis (CALM) extrapolation grade $γ$, a piecewise differentiable per-atom quantity integrated into GRACE foundation models and evaluated alongside energies and forces in a single model pass. We define $γ$ from nearest-cluster Mahalanobis distances in latent feature space, setting $γ=1$ from the training-distance distribution separately for each element and cluster. Controlled tests show that a normalized random projection of the invariant many-body basis detects structural and chemical extrapolation. On different foundation datasets, OMat24 and SMAX, $γ$ correlates with atomic force errors and separates structures with different error distributions. The CALM grade adds percent-level computational cost, and its spatial gradient guides uncertainty-biased data collection toward configurations with larger absolute force errors.

items.title: A methodological approach to wetsuit design based on the formation of a classification of water sports
items.abstract: This article is devoted to the development of methodological approaches to wetsuit design based on the classification of water sports. The goal of this research is to create innovative wetsuits adapted to the specifics of water sports, increasing reliability and protective properties, while improving comfort and performance. The subject of the study is the "person-wetsuit-aquatic environment" system, with a particular focus on protecting the wearer from external factors by developing rational variants of wetsuit components, taking into account ergonomics and the dynamic conformity of the product. The article proposes a systematic classification of aquatic sports, taking into account the nature of the aquatic environment, the degree of its control, temperature parameters, and the requirements for protective equipment. A model for the combination of the type of sports discipline and the characteristics of wetsuits (neoprene thickness, design, and mandatory application conditions) has been developed. Special attention was paid to the water sport "slalom" as a sport with maximum hydrodynamic variability and increased thermal protection requirements. The dependence of equipment selection on temperature ranges, flow velocity, and wind conditions has been substantiated. The presented classification can be used in the development of new types of wetsuits with enhanced protective properties, as well as in athlete training, regulatory requirements, and improvement of training logistics.

items.title: A multi-association rule-based knowledge graph method for exploring complex research trends in BIM
items.abstract: Traditional scientometric analysis methods primarily rely on binary keyword associations, which limits the ability to capture complex research structures. This study proposes a multi-association rule-based method (MAR) that enables the extraction of higher-order (n-ary) associations among keywords to address the stated limitation. The method integrates the Apriori algorithm with knowledge graph visualization to quantitatively analyse multi-keyword associations. The proposed method is applied to the Building Information Modelling (BIM) research domain. The bibliometric data, comprising 12,185 publications, is retrieved from the Scopus database following a systematic refinement of the initial search results to the architecture, engineering, construction, and operation (AECO)-relevant literature. The results demonstrate that the MAR method effectively identifies complex research patterns. The framework advances traditional scientometric tools by enabling the identification of multi-keyword semantic associations with quantified strength metrics (support, confidence, lift). Emerging trends revealed by the regression analysis include the convergence of BIM with generative artificial intelligence, real-time data integration, explainable AI, and human-centric approaches. The findings provide a scalable and analytical approach for identifying interdisciplinary research trends and gaps. The proposed method enables a deeper understanding of complex knowledge structures while supporting strategic decision-making and technology adoption.

items.title: A pilot-wellness-informed ecological framework for human-autonomy teaming in future fighter aviation
items.abstract: Future fighter operations are expected to combine increasingly capable autonomy, collaborative aircraft, dense sensor information, and sustained physiological and cognitive demands. This Perspective proposes a pilot-wellness-informed ecological framework in which the pilot, a pilot-specific digital twin, an intelligent flight-management system, the aircraft, and external agents are treated as interdependent elements within a systems-of-systems framework. The framework does not replace situation awareness, distributed cognition, joint cognitive systems, adaptive automation, or human-autonomy teaming. Instead, it extends their unit of analysis by making the pilot’s dynamic physiological and neurocognitive state, longitudinal variability, and health-related constraints explicit system variables and design objectives. The pilot digital twin is defined narrowly as an individualized state-estimation and forecasting capability, whereas the intelligent flight-management system integrates pilot, platform, mission, and environmental information to provide explainable recommendations and, where authorized, bounded adaptive action. We identify testable propositions concerning individualized prediction, adaptive support, shared situation awareness, trust calibration, and governance. The framework is prospective and requires validation in simulation, training, and operationally representative environments. Its purpose is to organize research toward systems that protect pilot agency, sustain performance, and preserve long-term health while exploiting increasingly autonomous teammates.

items.title: A Preliminary Evaluation of the e-Learning for Renal Applied Pharmacology Tool for Enhancing Pharmacology Learning: A Pilot Quasi-Experimental Study
items.abstract: Electronic learning (e-learning) or online learning in medical education has become increasingly prevalent, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, poor student engagement and reduced motivation are among the critical challenges associated with online learning. The e-learning for Renal Applied Pharmacology (e-RAP) is a new technology-enhanced learning tool that includes a nephron image augmented with several Quick Response (QR) codes. It allows students to access relevant QR-linked educational materials prepared by the teachers. This quasi-experimental pilot study examined whether use of the e-RAP tool was associated with differences in cognitive performance, engagement, and motivation among 105 preclinical medical students at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA), Malaysia. Participants in the intervention group (Year 2, n = 45) used the e-RAP tool, while the control group (Year 1, n = 60) received conventional teaching. Cognitive performance, engagement, and motivation scores were measured using pre- and posttest multiple-choice questions (MCQ), the Burch Engagement Survey for Students, and the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire, respectively. Both groups demonstrated improvements in mean cognitive scores from pre- to post-test MCQ, with greater gains in the intervention group than in the control group. The intervention group was also associated with higher emotional and cognitive engagement (both in and out of class) and higher scores in several motivational domains, including intrinsic value, cognitive strategy use, and selfregulation. Although groups differed by academic year, baseline knowledge was comparable. Taken together, these preliminary findings suggest that e-RAP use may be associated with differences in cognitive performance, engagement, and motivation.

items.title: A Reusable Semantic Web Framework for Evidence-Grounded Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments under the EU AI Act
items.abstract: The EU AI Act (Art. 27) requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to conduct Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments (FRIAs) before deployment, yet the evidence needed for credible assessments is fragmented across incompatible incident repositories, risk vocabularies, and legal texts. We present a reusable Semantic Web-based framework that consolidates this evidence for two high-risk public sector categories: employment and worker management (Annex III(4)) and access to essential public services (Annex III(5)(a)). A curated 150-record corpus is annotated along four axes using keyword, LLM, and hybrid methods and serialised as a SPARQL-queryable knowledge graph of 1,351 RDF triples. Five FRIA demonstration scenarios surface 103 records (68.7% coverage). Evaluation against a 69-record gold standard reveals that LLM-assisted classification of the employment domain achieves only $κ= 0.045$, a cautionary result for automated fairness-related evidence retrieval in this domain. All artefacts are released openly to support adoption by regulators, national authorities, and SMEs.

items.title: A Situational Awareness-Driven Human-Machine Interface Framework for Enhancing Operators’ Performance in Agricultural Robotic Teleoperation
items.abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing adoption of automated/autonomous guided vehicles (AGVs) in precision agriculture, existing human-machine interfaces (HMIs) remain function-centric, frequently neglecting the cognitive and user experience (UX) needs of non-technical operators. Consequently, current dashboards suffer from limited usability, high cognitive load, and reduced system transparency, increasing the risk of operator error. To address this gap within agricultural teleoperation interface design, this study presents a theory-driven HMI framework that systematically translates Endsley’s Situational Awareness (SA) theory (Perception, Comprehension, Projection) and ISO 9241 ergonomic principles into a structured three-panel AGV teleoperation interface. Unlike conventional function-oriented dashboards, the proposed framework organises interface components according to operator cognitive requirements to support information perception, comprehension, and projection during remote operation. A theory-driven agricultural teleoperation HMI framework was developed by translating cognitive and ergonomic principles into practical interface organization strategies. To formatively evaluate this SA-driven design architecture, we conducted a user-perception study with non-expert digitally literate participants (N = 20), evaluating three iterative HMI prototypes. The comparative results indicate that the SA-aligned layout received higher user ratings in perceived decision-support capability (SA3), cognitive workload reduction, and overall usability compared with baseline designs during formative evaluation. The study provides preliminary methodological guidance for agricultural teleoperation HMI design, while recognizing that objective operational validation with target agricultural users remains necessary.

items.title: A Structural Model of Artificial Intelligence Integration in Language Instruction: A Systematic Review of Mediating Pathways to Written English Proficiency Among EFL Learners
items.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) writing instruction, yet the mechanisms through which AI integration may improve written English proficiency (WEP) remain theoretically fragmented. Objective: This systematic review synthesises literature published within the 2018–2026 review window, together with foundational theoretical works, to develop a structural-equation-modelling (SEM) framework in which self-regulated learning (SRL), learner engagement, self-efficacy, and AI literacy operate as parallel and serial mediators between AI integration and WEP. Method: Following a structured thematic-synthesis approach, the reviewed literature was organised around four connected domains: AI-supported writing instruction, generative-AI adoption, learner and teacher perceptions, and self-regulated learning in AI-supported contexts. The synthesis then examined evidence for direct, mediating, and serial relationships among the focal constructs. Key findings: The literature provides partial support for the individual links connecting AI integration, the proposed mediators, and language-learning outcomes; however, these pathways are rarely tested within a single integrated model. Evidence for mediation remains fragmented, the proposed serial chain is largely untested, and Jordanian and broader Levantine contexts remain under-represented relative to East Asian and Gulf settings. Implications: The review proposes fourteen hypotheses: nine direct-effect hypotheses (H1–H9) and five mediation hypotheses (H10a–H10e), including one serial mediation chain, as a framework for future quantitative validation among English majors at public Jordanian universities.

items.title: A Study of Web 1.0 To Web 4.0: Evolution, Technologies, Applications and Future Directions
items.abstract: Abstract The World Wide Web has evolved from a predominantly static information environment into an increasingly interactive, semantic, distributed and intelligent digital ecosystem. The earlier study on Web 1.0 to Web 3.0 described the transition from the read-only web to the read-write social web and then toward the semantic web. This revised study extends that framework to Web 4.0 and examines the technological and conceptual changes across the four stages. Web 1.0 is characterized by static pages, one-way information delivery and limited user participation; Web 2.0 emphasizes interaction, user-generated content, social networking and web applications; Web 3.0 is associated with semantic interoperability, decentralized architectures, data ownership and intelligent processing; and Web 4.0 is increasingly discussed as an intelligent or symbiotic web in which artificial intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), cloud/edge computing, augmented and virtual reality, machine-to-machine communication and autonomous agents can interact with people and each other. The literature does not provide one universally accepted definition of Web 4.0, so this paper treats it as an emerging research and technology paradigm rather than a fixed technical standard. The study also discusses implications for libraries and information services, including intelligent discovery, personalized services, virtual assistance, semantic knowledge organization and human-machine collaboration. The paper concludes that the movement from Web 1.0 to Web 4.0 represents a shift from information access toward participation, meaning, intelligence and increasingly symbiotic interaction.

items.title: A STUDY ON AI ADOPTION AND EMPLOYEE SATISFACTION IN THE INDIAN HEALTHCARE SECTOR
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare systems is rapidly increasing in India, with the market estimated to grow from $0.83 billion in 2023 to $17.75 billion by 2032. Employee satisfaction remains a major concern that relevant studies in the healthcare sector have yet to address. This article explores how AI integration is affecting employee satisfaction in India’s healthcare industry. The healthcare industry faces a 60% shortage of digital skills; 47% of Indian healthcare workers are not digitally literate, and only 34% of organizations are advancing toward piloting AI projects, despite 86% having adopted AI. Implementation challenges include limited technical expertise among clinicians, the psychological burden of increased monitoring, poor rural infrastructure, data privacy concerns, and workforce constraints. For AI to succeed, it must be presented as a supplement to workers, not a replacement. This shift should include targeted training to address digital literacy gaps, governance that incorporates clinician input in system design, and ongoing staffing support. Existing evidence suggests that AI adoption may be associated with burnout and reduced employee satisfaction when it is not coupled with these integrated efforts. Beyond technical expertise, research highlights human-centered design, thorough training for healthcare professionals, and maintaining autonomy as key drivers of effective AI integration in healthcare in India. To benefit from AI, healthcare facilities in India must adopt modern technology. They must also prioritize staff well-being.

items.title: A study on the pathways through which pet ownership influences fertility intentions
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s low fertility rate, examining the impact of pet ownership on fertility intentions and its underlying mechanisms holds significant importance for enriching research on factors influencing fertility decisions and for understanding the complex relationship between modern lifestyles and reproductive choices. This study, grounded in self-determination theory, collected 551 valid samples through questionnaire surveys and employed structural equation modeling for analysis. Findings reveal that pet ownership not only positively associated with fertility intentions but also indirectly affects them through mediating variables such as fertility motivation, intrinsic needs, and emotional value. Pet ownership appears to individuals’ positive expectations toward parenthood by providing opportunities for daily care, emotional companionship, and responsibility-taking; simultaneously, the nurturing experience and emotional bonds cultivated through pet ownership activate individuals’ intrinsic motivation toward the role of “parenthood.” This may fulfill fundamental psychological needs such as autonomy, competence, and relatedness, thereby strengthening reproductive motivation. The positive emotional experiences and heightened confidence in family life derived from pet ownership may significantly reduce sensitivity to reproductive pressures, indirectly supporting the willingness to have children. This study provides theoretical support and empirical evidence for understanding the relationship between pet ownership and fertility intentions, as well as for formulating relevant policies.

items.title: A study on the relationship between teacher feedback types, self-efficacy, and intrinsic motivation among violin learners
items.abstract: Introduction To explore the psychological mechanisms of persistence in adult instrumental learning, this study investigates the associations among different types of teacher feedback, self-efficacy, and intrinsic motivation, and examines the moderating role of learning stages. Methods Using a cross-sectional survey design, scale and open-ended text data were collected from 743 adult violin learners. A moderated mediation model was tested through multiple regression and the Bootstrap method, supplemented by thematic analysis to provide a qualitative context. Results Data analysis indicates: (1) Positive feedback and constructive feedback are significantly and positively associated with intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.207, p < 0.001; β = 0.342, p < 0.001), while negative feedback shows a significant negative association ( β = −0.318, p < 0.001); (2) Self-efficacy demonstrates a significant partial mediating association between the three types of feedback and intrinsic motivation, with indirect effect estimates of 0.103, 0.098, and −0.097, respectively (95% CIs all exclude 0); (3) The learning stage significantly moderates the conditional indirect effects: as the learning stage advances, the indirect association of positive feedback on intrinsic motivation via self-efficacy gradually weakens (index of moderated mediation = −0.045), whereas the indirect association of constructive feedback gradually strengthens (index of moderated mediation = 0.038). Open-ended texts echo these statistical paths at the micro-level. Discussion The study shows that there are heterogeneous and dynamic statistical connections between teacher feedback and adult intrinsic motivation, and self-efficacy is a key pathway to understanding this connection. In practice, the provision of instructional feedback content should match the learners’ experience stage.

items.title: A Taxonomy of Human-AI Interaction Patterns in Agent-Based Operations Management
items.abstract: Abstract The increasing deployment of AI agents in operations management, spanning production scheduling, predictive maintenance, supply chain management, and energy systems, is progressively shifting automated systems from decision support tools to autonomous decision-making entities. Despite this transition, existing frameworks do not adequately characterize how humans and AI agents interact in operational decision-making contexts. This paper proposes a taxonomy of human-AI interaction patterns in agent-based operations management, developed through a theory-driven approach based on decision theory, control systems, human factors, and explainable AI research. The taxonomy articulates the interaction space along five analytically separable dimensions: Decision Trigger, Execution Authority, Human Entry Point, Human Influence and Interpretive Access. It identifies seven interaction patterns organized into four macro-patterns ordered by increasing AI operational autonomy. Illustrative examples drawn from scientific literature demonstrate the discriminative capacity of the taxonomy across heterogeneous operations management domains and agent architectures. The taxonomy provides researchers with an analytical instrument to characterize and compare human-AI decision loop configurations, and practitioners with a design reference for deliberate and accountable interaction choices in operational AI deployments.

items.title: A VR-Based Multimodal System for Assessing Presentation Integrity and Character Formation in Higher Education
items.abstract: Background. Artificial intelligence (AI) integration in online presentation assessment has expanded rapidly; however, existing facial emotion recognition systems in education remain largely focused on surveillance and behavioral monitoring, with limited validation against human judgment and insufficient attention to ethical and character-development dimensions. Purpose. This study aimed to develop and validate a virtual reality (VR)-based multimodal assessment framework for evaluating presentation integrity among higher education students. Method. A design science research approach was employed involving 64 students from two parallel classes (A1, n = 33; A2, n = 31) at a university in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Data from expert validation, technical performance evaluation, NASA-TLX, System Usability Scale, and lecturer assessments were analyzed using content validity analysis with modified kappa, classification metrics, Bland-Altman agreement analysis, and descriptive statistics. Novelty. This study introduces a human-centered AI-VR assessment approach that integrates facial emotion recognition, gaze detection, and cognitive load measurement into a reflective Presentation Integrity Index. Unlike conventional AI-based monitoring systems that generate binary judgments, the proposed framework emphasizes ethical interpretation by combining affective, behavioral, and cognitive indicators to support formative character-based assessment. Results. The framework demonstrated satisfactory content validity (S-CVI/Ave = 0.83), although refinement of several indicators was required. Emotion and gaze modules achieved accuracy levels of 85.3% and 89.0%, respectively. The Presentation Integrity Index showed 93.8% agreement with lecturer assessments, moderate cognitive load (NASA-TLX = 46.7), and good usability (SUS = 76.4). Conclusion. The proposed AI-VR framework provides an ethical and reflective approach for character-based presentation assessment while requiring broader validation involving multiple evaluators and diverse educational contexts.

items.title: Accident-based human reliability assessment of ship mooring Operations: An Entropy-SLIM framework
items.abstract: Mooring operations are among the most hazardous activities in maritime transportation and continue to cause injuries and fatalities. Although accident investigation reports provide information on contributing factors, their use in human reliability assessment (HRA) remains limited. This study proposes an accident-informed framework to estimate human error probability (HEP) in ship mooring operations by integrating the Success Likelihood Index Method (SLIM) with the Entropy Weight Method (EWM). Thirty-five accident investigation reports were analysed to identify performance shaping factors (PSFs) associated with human error. The PSFs were transformed into an occurrence matrix, weighted using entropy analysis, and incorporated into SLIM to estimate HEP values for tasks. The execution-related mechanism (T6.1) yielded a slightly higher accident-informed HEP than the perception-related mechanism (T6.3) (6.42 × 10 −4 vs. 5.67 × 10 −4 ) and a higher frequency-based risk contribution index (0.0122 vs. 0.00738). Within Task T6, two main failure mechanisms were identified: execution-related failures associated with line handling and perception-related failures associated with hazard recognition. items.title: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions
items.abstract: Mobile GUI Agents powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show promise in human-computer intelligence. However, current research primarily focuses on reactive task execution while lacking a comprehensive “understanding-prediction-execution” process for user intentions, which are the core requirements of active agents. In this paper, we propose the Act2Intention framework that builds an active mobile agent by integrating understanding, predicting user intentions, and executing decisions. Firstly, we constructed the Act2Intention Bench through collection and validated generation, comprising 72,511 intentions and over 700,000 actions across 52 apps, thereby establishing the first benchmark for evaluating proactive agents via continuous “intention-actions” trajectories. We further develop the Act2Intention Agent, achieving proactive services through Proactive-oriented Intention Understanding, Personalized Proactive Intention Prediction, and Experience-guided Intention Execution. Experimental results show that supervised fine-tuning on Act2Intention Bench yields absolute improvements of +32.0 Acc-S, +10.25 Acc-S, and +6.9 SSR points over non-fine-tuned counterparts under the same agent framework for intention understanding, prediction, and execution, respectively. This success underscores the necessity and value of the Act2Intention Bench, which establishes a standardized platform for developing and evaluating proactive agents and consequently paves the way for research on intention-driven human-computer interaction. To facilitate further research, we open-source our code and Act2Intention Bench at: npuNancy/Act2Intention.

items.title: Adoption Frequencies of Expert- Driven Learning-Based AI Taxonomy among R&D SMEs and Start-ups in Turkiye
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption is widely studied at the organizational level, yet much less is known about the specific algorithms organizations adopt and the reasons for these choices. This study investigates AI adoption among research-and-development (R&D) small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and start-ups in Turkiye through a proposed expert-driven, learning-domain-based taxonomy comprising 28 algorithms grouped into seven AI families. Survey data were collected from 36 organizations affiliated with the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce. Reliability and validity were established, and adoption was examined through descriptive statistics and non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney tests. At the algorithm level, Decision Trees, Neural Networks, Multilayer Perceptron, and Linear Regression were the most adopted, reflecting a preference for interpretable, structurally familiar methods, whereas Deep Q-Network, Policy Gradient, and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping were the least adopted. At the family level, Unsupervised Learning and Natural Language Processing ranked highest, while Reinforcement Learning and Autonomous Behavior recorded the lowest and most divergent adoption. Adoption also varied by sector—Financial/FinTech and Engineering/Defense showed the broadest portfolios and Healthcare and Commerce/e-Commerce the narrowest—with statistically significant cross-sector differences for Autonomous Behavior and Unsupervised Learning. Adoption range increased across organizational stages, peaking at post-incubation. The findings extend the Technology-Organization-Environment framework with diffusion of innovation and dynamic capability theory to the algorithm level and emphasize AI algorithms’ knowledge as a target for SMEs’ digital transformation.

items.title: Advancing Educational Assessment in The Era of Artificial Intelligence: Strategy for Digital Transformation
items.abstract: The swift evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is dramatically changing the landscape of education, especially when it comes to assessment. Traditional methods, which focus heavily on standardized tests and final evaluations, are falling short in capturing the complex cognitive, social, and digital skills that are essential in today’s world. This paper delves into the transformative power of AI in educational assessment and suggests a strategic framework for embracing digital change. By reviewing current literature, the study highlights AI-driven innovations like adaptive testing, automated grading, learning analytics, and competency-based assessment models. It also tackles important challenges such as ethical issues, algorithmic bias, data privacy, and maintaining academic integrity. The paper emphasizes that a comprehensive, policy-oriented, and pedagogically sound approach are crucial for effectively integrating AI into assessment systems. In the end, it offers practical strategies for institutions aiming to update their assessment practices in an AI-enhanced educational environment.

items.title: Advancing Nuclear Physics with Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) are becoming powerful tools in scientific research across various disciplines. In this review, we summarize recent progress in AI-assisted studies of nuclear structure and reaction observables, heavy-ion collisions and dense nuclear matter properties, many-body wave functions, experimental facilities and data analysis. This review focus on new progress since the last review in 2023, and machine learning in nuclear physics is evolving from purely data inferences to physics informed learning. Future directions on the integration of physical knowledge with modern learning architectures, large foundation models and other emerging methods are also reviewed. These developments suggest that AI is enabling and advancing new approaches towards most challenging nuclear physics problems.

items.title: Advertising the Sustainable Future: AI, Immersive Media and Behaviour Change for Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract Viksit Bharat 2047 will not be achieved through infrastructure and technology alone. Much of the change will be visible in ordinary routines: the way electricity and water are used at home, the way waste is handled, the products people choose, and the willingness of communities to take part in local environmental efforts. Advertising is relevant here because it already knows how to reach large audiences, tell memorable stories and influence everyday choices. Advertising itself is changing quickly. Artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), spatial computing and algorithmic personalisation are giving audiences more interactive forms of communication. This paper considers what these developments could mean for sustainability campaigns. The main concern is a familiar one: people may genuinely care about environmental issues and still struggle to turn that concern into consistent behaviour. The discussion draws on secondary material relating to the IndiaAI Mission, NITI Aayog policy directions, Sustainable Development Goal 12 and media-effects research. On this basis, the paper develops the AI-Immersive Sustainable Advertising Behaviour Model (AISABM). It brings together five connected ideas: context-sensitive communication, immersive experience, trustworthy information, a simple route to action, and feedback based on observable behaviour. Technology can also create a new divide if access is taken for granted. High-end VR is unlikely to be equally available to everyone, whereas radio, podcasts, smartphones and lightweight AR applications can travel much further. This is why the paper does not present immersive media as a replacement for older channels. It argues for a combination of both. The discussion also considers surveillance, manipulation, greenwashing and the energy cost of AI itself. The larger argument is that sustainability advertising has to do more than ask people to 'be green'. A useful campaign should make the issue understandable, connect it with everyday life, provide evidence people can trust and make the next step reasonably easy. Where possible, that step should also be observable over time.

items.title: Afterglow: A Place-Based Memorial Ecology for AI-Mediated Pet Bereavement
items.abstract: Pet bereavement often receives little social recognition. Generative AI can give a continuing bond a responsive voice, but a comforting reply may also claim authority to forgive or request attention. We investigate how a memorial can support connection without turning remembrance into obligation. Through Research through Design, we developed Afterglow, a mobile world connecting private remembrance, human witnessing, and symbolic Pet messages. A formative survey (N=57) informed the initial design, followed by six online roundtable walkthroughs with 20 unique participants across two prototype iterations. Our interpretive analysis develops tensions between returnable connection and emotional obligation, recognizable likeness and ontological clarity, and protective intervention and surveillant authority. We contribute Legible Restraint, a cross-layer requirement that limits on relational authority survive changes in speaker, generation context, trigger logic, data use, and participation. Its temporal consequence, Designing for Goodbye, keeps remembrance available without making continued use a condition of care.

items.title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training
items.abstract: An unsuccessful LLM agent rollout contains more information than its final reward: the observations available to the agent, the actions it chose, and the environment's responses. Reusing this experience for learning requires identifying a decision to revise and testing a concrete alternative. We introduce the Agent Error Dataset (AED), comprising 50,228 error-diagnosis pairs from 9,961 source tasks across 33 environments, 19 harness families, and 23 policy models in text-based agent systems. We retain source traces and execution metadata to support cross-setting failure analysis and re-diagnosis without repeating the original rollout. Our five-stage Agentic Error-to-Training (AET) pipeline collects natural failures, generates diagnoses and proposed corrections, and checks them against recorded evidence. Where replay is supported, we compare corrections with original-action retries from the same checkpoint under matched execution settings. We then construct separate training views for diagnosis and actor recovery. Across 3,062 matched replay pairs, first-proposal corrections raise verifier pass rates from 18.4% to 51.1%, a gain of 32.7 percentage points. Using a separately frozen diagnosis release, full-diagnosis fine-tuning on 1,656 source tasks raises Qwen3-8B's exact-step agreement with internal teacher labels from 47.2% to 63.6%, averaged over three seeds on a 943-case holdout. The strongest prompted reference in this comparison scores 54.7%, and mean agreement improves at each of four increasing training-set sizes. In a single-seed comparison of actor-training recipes, action-only repair training scores 6.67 percentage points higher on WebShop-lite than success-only training.

items.title: Agentic Modeling Framework for Materials‐to‐Device Cross‐Scale Design of Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have progressed rapidly over the past decade. As the core functional layer, the intrinsic properties of perovskite materials, including band structure, carrier transport, and optical response, strongly influence PSC performance. Theoretical calculations support absorber screening and device‐performance prediction. However, most studies remain confined to either materials‐level investigation or device‐level evaluation, without a general framework linking microscopic material properties to macroscopic device performance. To address this gap, we develop a large language model (LLM)‐driven, materials‐to‐device cross‐scale agentic framework that establishes a closed‐loop workflow from first‐principles descriptor extraction to solar‐cell performance optimization. A Manager Agent coordinates density functional theory (DFT)‐based materials calculations, drift‐diffusion device simulation, and Bayesian optimization of PSC architectures. Through the model context protocol (MCP), 55 in‐house tools and analysis/simulation programs are encapsulated and orchestrated as callable skills, enabling human‐in‐the‐loop review, cross‐scale parameter transfer, task‐state control, simulation execution, provenance tracking, and error recovery. Across 24 multi‐turn sessions and 60 benchmark turns, the agent achieved a pass rate of 96.7%, significantly outperforming OpenClaw (60.0%). This work provides an extensible methodological route for traceable, auditable, and closed‐loop cross‐scale research on PSCs.
